# Benchmark results (auto-generated by `python -m plainsboro.eval.analyze`)

Blind synthetic set, n = 240 targets. Stopping threshold 0.9, budget 5 tests / 10.0 cost units. All conditions replay identical precomputed test outcomes (matched conditions). 90% bootstrap CIs.

## Main comparison

| Condition | Accuracy | Mean cost | Mean tests | Cost-to-correct | Tests-to-correct | Brier | ECE | needs_human |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| B1 fixed checklist | 0.846 [0.81, 0.88] | 6.62 [6.57, 6.67] | 4.62 | 6.57 | 1.67 | 0.243 | 0.053 | 0.42 |
| B2 random order | 0.871 [0.83, 0.90] | 7.51 [7.32, 7.69] | 4.33 | 7.45 | 1.67 | 0.190 | 0.034 | 0.43 |
| B3 EIG planner only | 0.883 [0.85, 0.92] | 5.56 [5.38, 5.72] | 4.14 | 5.42 | 1.38 | 0.159 | 0.043 | 0.24 |
| P House team | 0.917 [0.89, 0.94] | 6.62 [6.44, 6.80] | 4.31 | 6.53 | 1.43 | 0.133 | 0.040 | 0.26 |
| P without Foreman | 0.896 [0.86, 0.93] | 6.27 [6.11, 6.42] | 4.34 | 6.22 | 1.43 | 0.153 | 0.037 | 0.27 |

Oracle (hindsight-optimal subset): 0.97 of targets solvable to >= 0.9 within budget, mean cost 4.04.

## Speedup at matched accuracy

Each condition's accuracy-vs-cost curve comes from its stopping-threshold sweep. Speedup = cost the baseline needs / cost the House team needs, both at the highest accuracy the two can reach (usually the baseline's ceiling). Ceiling = best accuracy reachable within the 5-test / 10-unit budget.

| Baseline | Matched accuracy | Speedup | 90% CI | Baseline ceiling | House ceiling | Ceiling gain 90% CI | Wilcoxon p (paired cost @0.9) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| B1 fixed checklist | 0.846 | 1.90x | [1.47, 2.39] | 0.846 | 0.917 | [0.03, 0.11] | 0.12 |
| B2 random order | 0.896 | 1.85x | [1.19, 2.08] | 0.896 | 0.917 | [-0.01, 0.04] | 6e-08 |
| B3 EIG planner only | 0.892 | 1.51x | [0.86, 1.64] | 0.892 | 0.917 | [0.00, 0.05] | 4.4e-25 |
